source.publication: 2025 Oklahoma Resident Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions (Form 511 packet)
source.section: Form 511 lines 1-14 and 18 (PDF pages 42-43); select line instructions (PDF pages 9-10); standard deduction line 10 (PDF page 10); exemptions line 11 and the Regular exemption terms (PDF pages 8 and 10); Tax Table (PDF pages 27-38); Schedule 511-A (form PDF page 45); Schedule 511-A line 5, Oklahoma Government or Federal Civil Service Retirement (PDF page 17)

worked: Federal AGI = California state public pension (you) 30,000.00 + Oklahoma public pension (spouse) 12,000.00 = 42,000.00. Federal taxable income = 42,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 = 10,500.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Oklahoma starts from federal AGI). Schedule 511-A: line 5: spouse 12,000.00 in federal AGI, limit 10,000.00, claims 10,000.00; line total 10,000.00; line 18 total subtractions 10,000.00 = 10,000.00. Form 511: line 1 federal AGI 42,000.00; line 2 subtractions 10,000.00; line 3 = 42,000.00 - 10,000.00 = 32,000.00; line 4 out-of-state income 0.00; line 5 32,000.00; line 6 additions 0.00; line 7 Oklahoma AGI 32,000.00; line 8 adjustments 0.00; line 9 32,000.00; line 10 standard deduction (married joint) 12,700.00; line 11 exemptions: 2 Regular + 0 Special = 2 x 1,000.00 = 2,000.00 (no one is 65 or older, 0 Special); line 12 = 12,700.00 + 2,000.00 = 14,700.00; line 13 taxable income = 32,000.00 - 14,700.00 = 17,300.00; line 14 tax (the projection's brackets as numbers; the booklet prints only a table and worksheets): 0.25% x 2,000.00 = 5.0000 + 0.75% x 3,000.00 = 22.5000 + 1.75% x 2,500.00 = 43.7500 + 2.75% x 2,300.00 = 63.2500 + 3.75% x 4,600.00 = 172.5000 + 4.75% x 2,900.00 = 137.7500; total 444.7500 = 444.75. Line 13 is under 100,000, so the form reads the tax table: row 17,300-17,350, column 'Married filing joint or head of household', PDF page 29, gives 446; expected keeps the schedule figure. Lines 15-17 credits 0.00; line 18 income tax 444.75. Your California pension gets nothing here; your spouse's Oklahoma pension gets 10,000.00 on line 5. If the California plan is a listed type, line 6 takes 10,000.00 of yours: tax 475.00 less.
accepted_approximations: The brackets are derived from the printed tax table and the 100,000-and-over worksheets; the booklet prints no schedule. Below 100,000 tax is figured on the exact income, where the booklet taxes each 50-dollar row at its midpoint and rounds. At 100,000 and over the single and separate worksheet starts from 4,562 where the schedule gives 4,561.50.

A pension from another state's government, New York State included, is left out of line 6 and taxed in full. Line 5's list does not name it; line 6 is a list of plan types and the booklet does not say which type another state's plan is (covers_unclear in the record). If the plan is a listed type, it qualifies under the shared 10,000 limit.
